strings.text: On price sensitivity: external research gives a reference range for eating out as a whole. Your actual customers may be more or less price-sensitive than that, and the High setting is a stress assumption rather than a research finding.
We compared three decisions using the same model of your cafe and the same assumptions. Only the decision changes between them — so the differences come from the decision, not from different guesses.
Cash is calculated from the model's daily orders, price and ingredient-cost outputs, using your sales, costs and cash figures below. Cash itself is not simulated directly.
Appointments served is the smaller of appointments wanted and the slots available — an identity about slots, applied after the model, never simulated.
The studies listed under “How this was calculated” are reference points our range was positioned against, not measurements of this trade.
Note: by cash at day 90, ${SHORT[rank[0]]} is ahead; by what each decision earns per month once things have settled, ${SHORT[byNet[0]]} is ahead.
The comparison stops at 90 days because that is as far as wages and rent can honestly be treated as fixed — not because the effects stop there.
Costs take about a week to rise — you are still using stock bought at the old price. Customers take a couple of weeks to react to a new price.
